PAPER 713
Hydrohalogenation Reaction of Substituted 1,2-Allenic Carboxylic Acids, 
Esters, Amides, Nitriles, and Diphenyl Phosphine Oxides
Shengming Ma,* Hexin Xie, Guangwei Wang, Junliang Zhang, Zhangjie Shi
Laboratory of Organometallic Chemistry, Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences, 354 Fenglin Lu, Shang-
hai 200032, P. R. China
Fax +86(21)64166128; E-mail: masm@pub.sioc.ac.cn
Received 27 September 2000; revised 12 January 2001
Synthesis 2001, No. 5, 12 04 2001. Article Identifier: 
1437-210X,E;2001,0,05,0713,0730,ftx,en;F05300SS.pdf. 
© Georg Thieme Verlag Stuttgart · New York
ISSN 0039-7881
Abstract: The hydrohalogenation reaction of 1,2-allenic carboxyl-
ic acids, esters, amides, nitriles, and diphenyl phosphine oxides with
HX or MX (X = I, Br, Cl, M = Na, Li) in different solvents, such
as HOAc, CF
3CO2H, and CF3CO2H-HOAc (1:1) was studied. The
reaction is a nucleophilic conjugate addition in nature and provides
efficient entries to 3-halo-3-enoic acids, esters, amides, nitriles, and
2-haloallyl diphenyl phosphine oxides. The /c98,/c103- over /c97,/c98-selectivity
and stereoselectivity depend on the solvent(s) and the temperature
applied. In most cases, the Z- and E-isomers can be easily separated
by chromatography on silica gel. The subsequent cross-coupling re-
action with organometallic reagents and terminal alkynes showed
the synthetic potential of these products.
Key words: electron-deficient allenes, hydrohalogenation, regiose-
lectivity, stereoselectivity, solvent effect
3-Alkenoic acids as well as their derivatives and 2-haloal-
lyl phosphine oxides are classes of compounds with syn-
thetic importance due to the uniquely located carbon-
carbon double bonds. Recently during the course of our
study on the chemistry of allene,
1,2 we developed the hy-
drohalogenation reaction of electron-deficient allenes, 3
such as 1,2-allenyl ketones, 4,5 carboxylic acids, 4 esters, 4
sulfoxides,6 and sulfones7 to afford /c98-halo-/c98,/c103-unsaturat-
ed functionalized alkenes. A challenge encountered here
is the potential migration of the C=C bond from the 
/c98-
halo-/c98,/c103-position to the /c97,/c98-position, thus, affording a
synthetically useless mixture of /c98,/c103-unsaturated products
and /c97,/c98-unsaturated products. 4,5,8 In a preliminary
communication9 we have demonstrated that the hydroha-
logenation reaction of 2-alkyl-2,3-dienoates with MX in
CF
3COOH-HOAc or CF3COOH afforded 2-alkyl-3-halo-
3-alkenoates with a high selectivity. Here, the reaction
medium is the key to avoid the formation of a mixture of
/c98,/c103-unsaturated and /c97,/c98-unsaturated products. In this pa-
per we wish to report our recent results of the hydrohalo-
genation reaction of differently substituted 2,3-dienoic
acids, esters, amides, nitriles, and 1,2-allenyl phosphine
oxides and the corresponding synthetic application of
the 
/c98,/c103-unsaturated 3-halo-3-alkenoates,  /c98,/c103-unsaturated
3-halo-2-alkenenitriles, and /c98,/c103-unsaturated 2-halo-2-
propenyl diphenyl oxides.

dienoic acid with NaI under different conditions are sum-
marized in Scheme 1.

The slow hydrohalogenation reaction of ethyl 2-methyl-
2,3-butadienoate with MX in HOAc afforded slowly a
mixture of 2-enoates and 3-enoates in low yields and se-
lectivity (Table 3). However, when a 1:1 mixture of
CF
3CO2H and HOAc or CF 3CO2H alone was used as the
reaction medium, the hydrohalogenation went smoothly
to afford ethyl 3-halo-2-methyl-3-butenoates in fairly
good yields and excellent selectivity (compare entries 1 –
5 with 6 –12, Table 3), while the corresponding reaction
with HX was reported to afford a mixture of 
/c98,/c103-unsatur-
ated alkenoate and /c97,/c98-unsaturated alkenoate.11 The reac-
tion in CF 3CO2H was much more efficient that in
CF3CO2H-HOAc (1:1) (compare entries 8 with 6 and 9
with 7, Table 3).
For trisubstituted allenes, i.e., 2,3-dienoates 3e-g, the re-
action also went smoothly to afford the corresponding
/c98,/c103-unsaturated 3-enoates 4 (Table 4). However, with 2,4-
disubstituted 2,3-dienoate 3e and 4,4-disubstituted 2,3-di-
enoate 3g, self-cyclization products, i.e., butenolides 6e
and 6g,12 were formed as the by-products along with the
expected hydrohalogenation products 4ec, 4ga and 4gb.
When fully substituted 2,3-dienoate 3h was treated with
MX in HOAc, self-cyclization affording butenolide 6h12
was the only reaction observed (Scheme 4).
Scheme 4
3-Halo-3-alkenoates are expected to be very useful syn-
thetic intermediates, due to the existing carbon-halogen
bond, ester group, carbon-carbon double bond, and the
acidic /c97-proton. The carbon-iodine bond in ethyl 2-meth-
yl-3-iodo-3-butenoate ( 4ca) was shown to cross-couple
with terminal alkynes13–15 and organozinc reagents15,16 un-
der catalytic conditions using Pd(0) to afford a series of
substituted 
/c98,/c103-unsaturated alkenoates (Scheme 5). Previ-
ously, 7b-type products were prepared via either the alky-
lation reaction of /c98-aryl-/c98-methyl acrylates 17 or
dehydration reaction of /c98-hydroxycarboxylic acids which
could be synthesized with a Reformatsky reaction,18 while
the syntheses of 7a- and 7c-type compounds have not
been reported so far.

In conclusion, we have developed a convenient method
for the synthesis of 3-halo-3-alkenoic acids, their deriva-
tives and 2-halo-2-propenyl diphenyl phosphine oxides
via a simple reaction of 2,3-dienoic acids, their deriva-
tives, and 1,2-allenyl diphenyl phosphine oxides with MX
in HOAc, CF
3CO2H-HOAc, or CF3CO2H. In most cases,
the yields are high; the stereoselectivity depends on the re-
action temperature and the solvent used; the ratios of 
/c98,/c103-
unsaturated and /c97,/c98-unsaturated products are determined
by the acidity of solvent used. The uniquely located C=C
bonds, C-X bonds, and the electron-withdrawing func-
tional groups make these products synthetically useful. In
most cases, the Z- and E-isomers can be readily separated
providing efficient entries to both relevent stereoisomers.
The reaction is nucleophilic in nature.
